summary.text: Leonardo da Vinci (1452 to 1519) was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance, active as a painter, engineer, scientist, sculptor and architect.
His fame first rested on painting, but his notebooks hold drawings and notes on anatomy, astronomy, botany, cartography and palaeontology.
Among his works are the Mona Lisa, regarded as the world's most famous painting, and The Last Supper, the most reproduced religious painting of all time.

facts.label: Last years
facts.value: Three years in France at Francis I's invitation

facts.label: Salvator Mundi
facts.value: Sold at auction in 2017 for US$450.3 million

items.prompt: Leonardo made real discoveries in anatomy, optics and geology. Why did they have little influence on the science that followed?

options.label: He wrote them only in Latin, which scientists could not read
He did not publish his findings
They were all proven wrong by other thinkers in his time
The Church ordered his notebooks destroyed after his death

items.explain: He made substantial discoveries but did not publish them, so they had little to no direct influence on subsequent science.

items.prompt: Leonardo sketched flying machines and an armoured fighting vehicle, yet few of his designs were built. Why?

options.label: He refused to share his drawings with anyone
Rulers of the time forbade the building of machines
Modern approaches to metallurgy and engineering were only in their infancy
He only ever drew machines as decoration for paintings

items.explain: Relatively few of his designs were constructed or feasible because modern scientific approaches to metallurgy and engineering were in their infancy.

items.prompt: A teenager joins Verrocchio's workshop in Florence. Why would the training reach beyond painting?

options.label: It mixed technical skills like metallurgy and mechanics with drawing and sculpting
It covered only drawing and painting, taught by a single master
It focused on writing and law, as in a notary's family
It was limited to theory taught in a lecture hall

items.explain: He was exposed to both theoretical training and a wide range of technical skills, including chemistry, metallurgy and mechanics, as well as drawing, painting and sculpting.

items.prompt: Many people first know Leonardo through one kind of work. What else is he known for beyond it?

options.label: A collection of published scientific books that taught later scholars
Notebooks full of drawings and notes on subjects such as anatomy and astronomy
A famous set of poems written for his patron Ludovico Sforza
A map of the New World drawn after he left Italy

items.explain: His fame initially rested on painting, but he is also known for notebooks with drawings and notes on a variety of subjects.

items.prompt: Most of Leonardo's grand designs stayed on paper. What happened to some of his smaller ones?

options.label: They were patented and credited to him in his lifetime
They were lost when his workshop burned
They were copied only by his half-siblings
Some, like an automated bobbin winder, entered manufacturing unheralded

items.explain: Some smaller inventions, such as an automated bobbin winder and a wire-strength testing machine, entered the world of manufacturing unheralded.

items.prompt: Where did Leonardo end his life, and what brought him there?

options.label: France, where he went at the invitation of Francis I
Rome, where he went to serve the pope
Milan, where Ludovico Sforza kept him in service
Vinci, where he returned to his family's land

items.explain: On the invitation of Francis I, he spent his last three years in France, where he died in 1519.
